# A finite-rectangle reflection theorem and depth-two collapse for all compact locales

22 October 2026.

**THEOREM (finite rectangular cover reflection).** Let L be an arbitrary frame and a_i,b_i∈L (i=1,...,n). If
    1_(L⊕L)=∨_{i=1}^n (a_i⊠b_i),
then the finite family of pairs {(a_i,b_i)} admits an H→V separation tree of edge depth at most TWO, with precisely these pairs as terminal leaves (allowing coordinatewise restrictions).

**Proof.** Let K be the sublattice generated by 0,1 and the finitely many a_i,b_i under finite meets and joins. The free distributive lattice on finitely many generators is finite, so K is finite. Inclusion K→L is an injective frame homomorphism (arbitrary joins in a finite K reduce to finite joins). Regard K as O(Y), where Y is a finite T0 Alexandrov space.

First prove that the induced homomorphism K⊕K→L⊕L reflects a top-cover of any family of rectangles with coordinates in K. For each y∈Y let U_y be its least open neighborhood and V_y=U_y\{y}; both are opens of Y and U_y>V_y in K. Under the inclusion into L, the locally closed sublocale
    F_y=O_L(U_y) ∩ C_L(V_y)
is nonzero (the open U_y is not below V_y). Every a∈K restricts to 1 on F_y when y∈a (since U_y≤a), and to 0 on F_y when y∉a (since a∧U_y≤V_y). For every y,z, the localic product F_y×_loc F_z is nonzero: coproducts of two nontrivial frames are nontrivial (also immediate from rectangular C-ideal representation). Its map into X×_loc X pulls back each a_i⊠b_i to either 0 or 1 depending on whether (y,z)∈a_i×b_i. If the rectangles cover 1_(L⊕L), then at least one must be top for each pair (y,z), so the same finite rectangles cover all points of Y×Y. As finite locale products are spatial, they cover 1_(K⊕K).

Now construct an H→V proof. Root horizontal cover 1=∨_{y∈Y}U_y. For any fixed y, the opens b_i with y∈a_i cover Y, as the rectangles cover Y×Y. Since U_y≤a_i whenever y∈a_i, split (U_y,1) vertically into (U_y,b_i), each a leaf below (a_i,b_i). Maximum two cover edges. Thus finite-rectangle cover reflection and rank≤2.

**COROLLARY (compact locales).** If L has compact top, then every rectangular bar B⊆L×L, meaning d∨b_B=1 in L⊕L, admits a separation tree of depth≤2.

Proof. Localic Tychonoff theorem: the localic product of compact locales is compact, equivalently 1_(L⊕L) is compact. Because d and b_B are joins of rectangles from D={(a,b):a∧b=0} and B, respectively, compactness extracts finitely many pairs from D∪B with join of their rectangles =1_(L⊕L). Apply the theorem above. All leaves are in D or B.

**SIGNIFICANCE.** This extends earlier depth-two result for compact SPATIAL locales to arbitrary compact locales, including nonspatial ones. It strengthens the previous compact-top transpose absorption result: no compact-top frame admits a rectangular bar of minimum rank≥3, irrespective of symmetry. The rank-three rational-bridge examples necessarily have noncompact top. The result does NOT prove (*) for arbitrary noncompact frames. It also explains why finitary tensor-cover evidence cannot witness rank three or higher even in a noncontinuous frame.

**Checks:** The argument must not replace localic product by the ordinary product of point spaces. The finite point space Y is used only for finite K; locally closed F_y inside the possibly pointless X is required to reflect the cover. F_y×F_z nonzero relies on general locale product nontriviality, not existence of ordinary points of X. External reference for compact product: localic Tychonoff theorem (Johnstone-Vickers; https://ncatlab.org/toddtrimble/published/Tychonoff%2Btheorem%2Bfor%2Blocales).
